lessons.title: Question: Exception handling
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why might we want to use a try and except block?

To allow our program to handle errors effectively and continue runningTo write conditional statements

To allow our program to handle errors effectively and continue running.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A try and except block lets a program handle errors effectively and continue running.

A record lookup may fail, but the program must display a fallback and continue. Why use these blocks?

The except block can handle the lookup error and let later code run.The blocks guarantee that the lookup always succeeds.The blocks turn the lookup into a conditional statement with no errors.

The except block can handle the lookup error and let later code run.

lessons.title: Question: Uncertain operations
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of the following situations might we use a try and except block for?

When we are not sure whether the user input will be validWhen we are not sure of whether Python allows a particular operation

When we are not sure whether the user input will be valid.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We might use a try and except block when we are not sure whether the user input will be valid.

Which task is a good use for these blocks?

Converting typed user text to a number when the text may contain lettersAdding two fixed numeric values that the programmer already controlsChoosing a clearer variable name for a known value

Converting typed user text to a number when the text may contain letters.

lessons.title: Question: The `pass` keyword
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when the pass keyword is executed?

Nothing - Python moves on to the next code blockPython prints the last stored variable

Nothing - Python moves on to the next code block.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When pass executes, it does nothing and Python moves on to the next code block.

An except block contains only pass, followed by print("Done"). What displays after an error is caught?

DoneThe caught error, because pass raises it againThe last variable stored before the error

Make sure to pick Done.

lessons.title: Question: The `raise` keyword
lessons.interactiveContent:

When we want to highlight that an error has occurredWhen we want to increase the value of a variable

When we want to highlight that an error has occurred.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use raise when we want to highlight that an error has occurred.

An age validator receives -4. Which line explicitly signals the invalid value?

raise ValueError("Age cannot be negative")age += 1pass

raise ValueError("Age cannot be negative").

lessons.title: Question: `finally` statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
When should the finally statement be used?

At the end of a try and except block, to execute code whether or not an exception occurredTo highlight the last line of a program to be executed

At the end of a try and except block, to execute code whether or not an exception occurred.
lessons.hardModeContent:
At the end of try and except, a finally block runs whether or not an exception occurred.

A file must be closed after a read succeeds or fails. Where should the cleanup code go?

In the finally blockOnly in the try blockOnly in the except block

Make sure to pick In the finally block.
